title: PRESSER | Chris Beard - Nicholls Postgame (11-17-26)
text: couple of things. U looks like a a trademark of your team's less than double digit turnovers. I know you got to be proud of that. >> Yeah, it's been been a big part of our success over the years. Um currently at Old Miss, you know, we just it's kind of captain obvious, but we we want to score and uh if we give the ball to the other team, we don't have a chance to score, we don't have a chance to get fouled, we don't have a chance to get an offensive rebound. And so, and I think this year's team's embracing it. You know, it starts with the playmakers, Bud and Ilas. And then I think u several positives tonight. I I think um our fan base got to see um what Ben can do, you know, with the ball in his hands. Ben's a playmaker as well. So this this year continues, you're you're basically playing with three playmakers on the floor uh with Ben, Ilas, and Bud. >> What about is something wrong with Connor? >> Yeah. uh ankle this week practice got himself back on the practice floor and then just made a game day decision um trying to get him back to closer to 100% for Maui. Uh but he did a really good job as a young player this week kind of mentally choosing to play practicing all the way until this morning's shootound and then uh John Raybond who I trust as much as anybody I've ever worked with you know made that decision which I think was the right one. Um maybe we can get yo back closer to 100% by Maui. follow up on earlier question. How do you feel about stepping up in competition? Is your team ready? >> Uh we'll see. U yet to be determined. You know, I I I kind of approach each game like it's the biggest game I've ever coached in. U but I recognize the question as well. Um you know, we're proud to take the Old Miss brand to Maui. First time Old Miss has ever played in in one of, if not the most prestigious, you know, non-conference tournament. I know we got some rivals in that space today, but there's still no denying what what Maui is. So, I'm excited for our players to have this experience. I'm excited for Old Miss to be able to play on this stage. Um, you know, we look forward to the opportunity. It's going to be three basic, you know, NCA tournament BCS power four games. >> Coach, you've got to be pleased on your 300th win with the rebound totes. >> Yeah, I think uh I didn't know anything about the 300 until I think earlier this morning, and I appreciate Keith coming in. Um, I don't say this in a self-s serving way. I say this to understand there's a lot of players that played with for us before division one. So, we got a few more than 300 wins. Those wins at Angelo State and Fort Scott and Simol and South Carolina counted too. But um no, when you get any kind of like attention to that makes you pause for a quick second and then I just think about all those players at Little Rock, all those players at Tech and Texas and now here. You know, those guys and when a coach gets a game ball like that, there should be every name of every player that played for him. Uh you mentioned rebounding. That was a positive tonight. You know, our goal is to get 14 or 15 offensive rebounds every game. Tonight, we got to that point. Now, I think our poor three-point shooting tonight gave us a few more opportunities, so I have to study the film. But I do know it was a focus. Um, you know, you know what's important uh based on what the players are talking about in that locker room. And so there was more emphasis this week all the way up until game time and including halftime that our crashers had to produce tonight. So I think to get what 18 offensive rebounds and a couple extra loose balls, that's a good sign. >> Coach, you uh you had 24 points off turnovers and forced 21 turnovers. Was that something that you came into the game trying to do to force turnovers like that or was that just a natural byproduct of the game and how it developed? >> No, I think uh Roman said it best. It's a part of our identity. You know, there's different ways to play defense, right? In football, you going to stop the run, you going to stop the explosive play, and everybody's got a different identity. And so with this year's team, uh with the talent, the athleticism, and really the coaching staff as well, got a lot of great basketball minds that are contributing to this. Um we want to be a team that, you know, tries to put pressure on the defense. We want we want to be a team that tries to turn you over. Um and I think tonight we did a good job of that. Again, ear early season. We'll see how this plays out. Um but we we have shown an ability to turn the other team over. >> Chris, the guys just seem more aggressive this year. What have you seen? >> Yeah, I agree. Um starts with just some personalities, you know, like a Roman um saw him dive over that opponent bench like that. You know, it's only a few players in the country that are willing to do that. And um you know, I hope I hope that our home crowd understands that too. That that's a play that we don't teach or coach. That's a play that Roman chooses to make. So I think that kind of inspired our team um a lot. And I'd like to get to the point where that inspires our fan base as well. When a guy makes an unselfish, hard play and play like that. Uh Ben's a feisty guy. Bud's a competitor. I'm on the record. U we just added a lot of internally competitive people. I think that's bled into the team. Um, but yeah, I want I I'd much rather have a team that you got to pause it, turn it down a little bit from time to time than have to sit here and try to turn it up. Um, and we do not have to turn these guys up. Um, guys have seen some of our practices. Um, you understand like every single day we're competitive group. >> Coach, you talked about uh, you know, the player chemistry a lot throughout the early part of the season, but you have a lot of new coaching staff members as well. How have you seen the chemistry between your coaching staff kind of develop in the early part of this season? >> Yeah, it's a good question. We obviously have some some Hall of Fame type resumes. Got a couple guys on the staff that are in selective hall of fames, but you know, we all understand what Mark Adams has done in basketball and Brian Berg's been a division one head coach. Al's been doing this for a long time. Future division one head coach. Um I think at the end of this season, if we do what we're supposed to do on the court, Al's going to have some opportunities. You guys understand uh Peter Petar is one of the best coaches in the world. Um, FOB comes to us as a as is a veteran, man. He's coached a lot of different levels, impacted winning. Guys might, you know, be familiar with the Sam Houston State success the last couple years, not only their team, but some of their individual players going on becoming pros. And so, sure, I've left out a couple guys. Is been doing this a long time. Um, so just like putting a team together, you know, it's not just about getting 15 five stars. It's about the pieces have to fit. And I think our staff does a really good job. you know, we uh we disagree a lot. We get after it a lot and when we walk out of that room, we all align. Um this this group's been a lot of fun to work with so far, and I'm very appreciative of our staff. We have some real veterans. Appreciate that question. >> Have you honed down your rotation a little bit or is it still a work in progress? >> Yeah, I think it's a work in progress still. We're giving guys opportunities. You know, Zack earned some first half minutes tonight based on his practice performance. It was good to see Seir come in there and make a couple plays. Um, obviously Geron got an opportunity tonight and so yeah, I mean this is um this a competitive world and um we're never going to be set in stone. There's opportunity every day in everything we do to catch somebody's eyes and like I tell the players all the time, you know, make me play um you know, make me play. Make it where I look like a fool if I don't put you in the game. And so and through these first four games and really our three exhibition games as well, you guys have seen kind of the balance. Guys get some opportunities and it's up to them to take advantage of the opportunity when they get it. >> Obviously some pretty prestigious schools that you could potentially face in any early scouting report that you have on any of the teams you could face next week. >> Yeah, for sure. We go, you know, one game at a time. Um but we obviously have a staff. We can kind of prepare. No different than when you get to a NCA tournament. Um we turn these things into four team tournaments. It's the way we've always done it. So, there's four teams in our tournament. Uh the first two games, you know, we'll play a championship game on Tuesday. Um and then when you get to the third game, you know, it's u money in the bank or hay in the barn like Coach Knight used to say. And so, yeah, we got an early look at some of these teams. I personally have not I'm a basketball, you know, kind of fan. I got a problem. I mean, I really do. Um and so I've seen Washington play. I've seen Clemson play. I've seen BYU play. I've seen everybody play. Um, and so yeah, we'll start with that tomorrow. We'll uh we'll close the door on this game like we always do. Uh, you know, we try to explain to the guys we are more important than anybody we play. So, we'll learn from tonight's game and then we'll start, you know, we'll start talking about our first opponent, Maui, um, you know, tomorrow afternoon. >> Any concerns with three-point shooting? >> Uh, no. I think, uh, to me, you know, you put in the work. Um, concerns come if we're not getting the three-point shots. Concerns come if guys are losing confidence, which I don't think is the case. And so three-point shots a weapon, no doubt about it. Um, but it's not a weapon you can count on every single night. So, what you got to do on a night like tonight is you got to produce offensive rebounds from those long misses. And the stat sheet says we did. Um, but I I'll have to take a look at to see if if what happened really happened. I think that we got some better rebounding tonight because we were missing threes, but we'll see. But we got good shooters. I think as this thing plays out, we could be a team that ends up with four or five guys in that green light club, which is around 40% shooting. >> Coach, as a basketball junkie, who's been your favorite team to watch this season schematically or just, you know, talentwise in college basketball? >> Uh, that's a good question. Uh, I about favorite, you know, I always watch the guys that have been in our organization. You I don't miss a UTEP game. I don't miss an Abene Christian game. Um, you know, watching what Wes and those guys are doing out of Georgia Tech. That's kind of where my eye goes first. um is guys that have been in our organization. Um you know, Brad's a a friend at Illinois. We go back to the Jo days against each other. Dodge City, Fort Scott backgrounds, Daytona seminal backgrounds. And so I think the Illinois team has been, you know, just kind of fun to watch. It's my understanding they got a big win tonight. Doesn't surprise me. >> Thanks. >> Appreciate it, guys.
